title: The first version of the admin app is still kept in the code but nothing opens it
what: About 800 lines from the first read-only admin app (its sign-in, gym setup, dashboard, members table, data loaders and helpers) sit next to today's app. The start-up file opens only today's app, so none of it runs and no test covers it. It carries its own rule for an 'at risk' member (no activity for 7 days) that differs from the 'losing the habit' rule today's app uses, and it still calls the old gym-creation step that is open to every account.
expected: Old code nothing opens is removed, or clearly parked outside the app with one written plan for when it comes back; one rule decides who is at risk.
fix_line: Delete the old admin app files, or move them out of the app with a note, and keep one at-risk rule

title: Four separate copies of the 'read a picture' step have already drifted apart
what: The logo upload, the web page photos, the shop photos and the desk camera each carry their own copy of the step that opens a picked picture. The three photo copies ask the browser to turn a sideways phone photo upright and write a note when it fails; the logo copy asks for neither and fails silently before trying the fallback. A fix made in one copy does not reach the others.
expected: One shared picture-reading step used by all four uploads, with the same turn-upright and logging behaviour.
who: developers, and owners uploading a sideways logo photo
fix_line: Move the picture-reading step into one shared helper and use it in all four places

title: The Branding 'unsaved colour survives a refresh' test waits on the real clock for 16 seconds
what: The browser test that proves an owner's unsaved colour is not wiped by the 15-second refresh simply waits about 19 seconds of real time, then checks. It never confirms the refresh actually happened. On a slow test machine the refresh can land after the check, and the test still passes without testing the thing it was written for. It also adds about 19 seconds to every run.
expected: The test moves a fake clock past the refresh, or waits until it sees the refresh request, then checks the colour is still there.
fix_line: Use a fake clock or wait for the refresh request instead of fixed waits
